segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
A pedestrian
shall not cross an intersection diagonally
unless authorized by official traffic-control devices.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrian' is defined by DEF-NRS-484A-165 ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); the run admits it as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, claimed whole and never expanded into class atoms.

'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105: 'The area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines') is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'; the alley-junction exclusion of the definition's (3) is made by the atom's own contract. rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors the pedestrian in that intersection. 'diagonally' is a direction of the pedestrian's motion relative to the ways that meet there: the lanes that run into the intersection are read through st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; kind st.lane), and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier, whose contract compares the road user's velocity with a carrier's designated direction, is read at two tolerances on every such lane: across it with the tolerance that tells across from along, and not across it with the right-angle tolerance, so the motion is oblique to both crossing ways. st.lane_enters is not used for the subject's presence (that is rel.occupies) nor for governance.

An 'official traffic-control device' (DEF-NRS-484A-145) includes every 'marking ... placed or erected by a public authority ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the marking that authorizes a pedestrian crossing is a crosswalk 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings on the surface' (DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2)), carried by st.crosswalk ('marked crossing ...; marked attribute') read with its marked attribute; rel.occupies anchors the pedestrian inside that marked crossing. st.crosswalk 'Not a stand-in for' clauses do not concern this use.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) into which at least one lane runs (st.lane_enters); the duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
obligation: At each such observation: if the subject moves diagonally across x, that is, for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with parameters (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos), then the subject's footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk with its marked attribute true). Otherwise compliant.

narrowings.why: 'cross ... diagonally' is read at each observation as the pedestrian, inside the intersection, moving oblique to every lane that runs into it (neither within the right-angle tolerance of across a lane nor along it); a crossing is judged by its motion at each observation, not as a corner-to-corner path.
'official' is read through the presence of the marking on the road: a marked crosswalk in the scene is presumed placed by a public authority.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Lanes running into intersection x run north-south and east-west; a pedestrian inside x walks north-east at 1.4 m/s, oblique to every entering lane, with no crosswalk under its footprint.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x near its edge walks east at 1.4 m/s: across the north-south lanes at right angles, so the motion is not diagonal.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along a sidewalk and its footprint overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian is inside x with no marked crosswalk under it, but its velocity is not observed, so whether it moves diagonally cannot be told.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian inside x walks north-east within a marked diagonal crosswalk.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

segmentation.text: Except as provided in NRS 484B.290 [LVMC-11-30-140-B]:
When authorized to cross diagonally,
pedestrians
shall cross only in accordance with the official traffic-control devices pertaining to such crossing movements.

elements.justification: 'cross diagonally' is read as in NRS_484B_287_1d: the pedestrian's footprint overlaps an intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') and its velocity is oblique to every lane that runs into it (st.lane_enters, kind st.lane), read through drv.motion.moving_across_carrier at the along/across tolerance and the right-angle tolerance. 'authorized' by official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device') is read through the marking that indicates the crossing: a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing'; DEF-NRS-484A-065 (2) 'distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings') under the pedestrian's footprint. The crossing begins where the footprint comes to overlap the intersection.
'pedestrians' (DEF-NRS-484A-165: 'a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...') is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The devices 'pertaining to such crossing movements' that regulate a pedestrian's crossing are pedestrian signal heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'). The head pertaining to the pedestrian's diagonal movement is the one the pedestrian faces across the crossing: its position (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as a stop line or crossing, which its 'Not a stand-in for' clause excludes. 'in accordance with' is read through the indication shown when the crossing begins: walk, or a flashing indication with a countdown, accords; a steady don't-walk or a flashing one without countdown does not.

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) beginning an authorized diagonal crossing: at this observation its footprint comes to overlap an intersection x (rel.occupies, st.intersection) that it did not overlap at the previous observation, its footprint overlaps a marked crosswalk (st.crosswalk, marked), and it moves diagonally across x: for every lane l with st.lane_enters(l, x) (at least one exists), drv_motion_moving_across_carrier(subject, l) holds with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) and does not hold with (p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.right_angle_crossing_cos). The duty does not apply where LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject.
obligation: For every pedestrian signal head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) that the subject faces at this observation, d shows neither dont_walk_steady nor dont_walk_flashing without its countdown attribute. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from the subject's kin.position to d's dev.position and h the subject's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where no head is faced, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'official' is read through the presence of the signal head in the scene.

'cross only in accordance with the devices' is read at the start of the diagonal crossing (the entry into the intersection) through the indication of the pedestrian signal heads the pedestrian faces: a steady don't-walk, or a flashing don't-walk with no countdown, forbids starting; conduct later in the crossing is not read, and devices other than pedestrian signal heads are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: At an intersection with a marked diagonal crosswalk, a pedestrian steps from the corner into the intersection walking north-east inside the marking while the pedestrian head ahead of it, 25 m away within the facing cone, shows dont_walk_steady.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same entry, while the faced head shows walk.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian enters the intersection walking east, at right angles to the north-south lanes: no diagonal crossing begins.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same entry as forbid, but the state of the faced pedestrian head is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head shows dont_walk_flashing with its countdown displayed.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Same entry while the faced head shows dont_walk_flashing without a countdown.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.right_angle_crossing_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the motion counts as at right angles to the curb: within about 15 degrees of perpendicular
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability in naturalistic crossing studies

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

segmentation.text: When official traffic-control devices are not in place or not in operation,
the driver of a vehicle
shall yield the right-of-way,
slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield,
to a pedestrian crossing the highway within a crosswalk
when the pedestrian is upon the half of the highway upon which the vehicle is traveling or onto which the vehicle is turning,
or when the pedestrian is approaching so closely from the opposite half of the highway as to be in danger.

As used in this section, “half of the highway” means all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction, and includes the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway.

elements.justification: The official traffic-control devices (DEF-NRS-484A-145: every 'sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic') that regulate a crosswalk crossing are the vehicular signal heads (dev.traffic_signal, state including 'dark') and pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal, state including 'dark') that control the travel regions the vehicle and the pedestrian are in: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'), with rel.occupies anchoring each road user in a governed region (kind st.travel_region). 'not in operation' is a head showing 'dark' or dev.inoperative ('a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'); 'not in place' is no such head governing those regions. dev.governs is used for control, not for a position, as its exclusion requires.

'the driver of a vehicle' maps, as in the run's index, to the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions decided by the reading); 'driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a role, read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

Yielding the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian: no rel.contact ('the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap') and the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard below sets; as mapped in the run's index for 'shall yield the right-of-way'.

'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'crossing the highway within a crosswalk': the crosswalk (DEF-NRS-484A-065: 'That part of a highway at an intersection included within the connections of the lateral lines of the sidewalks ... or (2) Any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing') is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), marked or unmarked, so the definition's whole extent is kept; rel.occupies places the pedestrian's footprint in it.

By the section's own definition, a half of the highway is 'all traffic lanes ... designated for traffic traveling in one direction': the pedestrian's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane) or a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') whose designated direction (st.lane_direction, 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in') points with the vehicle's heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'): the half on which the vehicle travels, or, while it turns, the half its heading has turned onto. kin.heading is read as the direction of travel of a vehicle driven forward; st.lane 'Not a stand-in for' a half of the roadway does not apply because the half is assembled from the lanes' designated directions, as the definition itself builds it.

The section's definition of 'half of the highway' ('all traffic lanes of a highway which are designated for traffic traveling in one direction', 'the entire highway in the case of a one-way highway') is carried by the lanes (st.lane) grouped by their designated direction (st.lane_direction) and by a one-way roadway (st.one_way_roadway, 'roadway on which traffic is restricted to one direction'), the atoms c3 and st2 read.

operationalizations.standard: slowing down or stopping if need be so to yield (the right-of-way's 'danger of a crash unless one grants precedence')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash the driver has not yielded to; a vehicle at rest has slowed or stopped as need be

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely from the opposite half as to be in danger
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a pedestrian in the crosswalk on a lane whose designated direction points against the vehicle's heading is in danger where the predicted closest approach of the two centres falls within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. Devices are not in place or not in operation: every traffic signal head (dev.traffic_signal) that governs (dev.governs) a travel region the subject occupies shows dark or is inoperative (dev.inoperative). There is a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) whose footprint overlaps a crosswalk (st.crosswalk), such that every pedestrian signal head governing a travel region p occupies shows dark, p is not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B, and either (a) p's footprint overlaps a lane or one-way roadway whose designated direction (st.lane_direction) has a positive dot product with the subject's heading (kin.heading) — the subject's half — or (b) otherwise (p on the opposite half) the predicted closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).
obligation: For every such pedestrian p: the subject is not in contact with p (rel.contact), and where the subject's speed (kin.speed) is above p.halt_speed_tolerance, it is not the case that the closest approach of the subject and p falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.
'official' is read through the presence of the signal heads in the scene.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian stands in an unmarked crosswalk on a lane whose direction matches the subject's heading, 15 m ahead; the subject moves at 10 m/s with a predicted closest approach of 0.5 m in 1.5 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene, but the subject is at rest (speed 0.0 m/s) before the crosswalk while the pedestrian crosses its half.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A traffic signal head governing the subject's lane shows circular_green: the devices are in operation.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: No signal head governs the subject's lane; a pedestrian near the crosswalk is on the predicted collision course, but whether its footprint overlaps the crosswalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No signal heads and no pedestrian anywhere in the scene: the duty is decided for the subject alone as not engaged.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian in the crosswalk on the opposite half, on a lane whose direction points against the subject's heading, with no predicted closest approach within the horizon.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channel

segmentation.text: A pedestrian
shall not suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle
which is so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield.

elements.justification: 'A pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...').

Leaving 'a curb or other place of safety' is the pedestrian's footprint (rel.occupies) coming onto the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') from a place pedestrians are safe from vehicles: the sidewalk the curb bounds (st.sidewalk, 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'), a safety zone (st.safety_zone, 'an area within the highway marked off for pedestrians only') or a median or dividing section (st.median_or_divider). st.sidewalk is not used for a crosswalk, as its exclusion requires; st.roadway is not used for the sidewalk. 'into the path of a vehicle': the vehicle is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the pedestrian is in its path where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). These primitives are 'Not a stand-in for' contact or danger alone; here they bound the path the vehicle will sweep, the clearance and horizon set by the reading, and the impossibility is decided by the standard.

operationalizations.standard: so close that it is impossible for the driver to yield
operationalizations.convention: stopping-distance model: the vehicle cannot yield where the time to the predicted closest approach (prim.closest_approach_time) is less than the driver's perception-reaction time plus the vehicle's speed (kin.speed) divided by twice the braking deceleration, written as a product (2·a·t_ca < 2·a·t_r + v); the deceleration is selected by the surface: icy or snow-covered (env.ice_or_snow), else wet (env.wet_road), else dry

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) that leaves a place of safety at this observation: its footprint overlaps a roadway (st.roadway) here, and at the previous observation it overlapped no roadway and overlapped a sidewalk, a safety zone or a median or divider. The duty does not apply where NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2 is engaged for the subject, nor where LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2 is engaged for a vehicle v of the scene.
obligation: There is no vehicle v (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) such that the closest approach of the subject and v falls within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance) and 2·a·t < 2·a·p.driver_reaction_time + speed(v), where t is prim.closest_approach_time with horizon p.conflict_horizon, speed(v) is v's kin.speed, and a is p.following_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.following_decel_wet where env.wet_road holds, else p.following_decel_dry. With no vehicle in the scene, compliant.

narrowings.why: 'suddenly' is read through the vehicle's closeness at the moment the pedestrian leaves the place of safety: a departure is sudden in the law's sense where the vehicle is already too close to yield; the pedestrian's own abruptness is not measured.
'other place of safety' is read only through the sidewalk the curb bounds, a safety zone and a median or dividing section.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's motion: whether the vehicle can stop, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Dry road. The pedestrian steps from the sidewalk onto the roadway while a car 12 m away moves toward it at 12 m/s; predicted closest approach 0.5 m in 1.0 s, below 1.5 s + 12/(2·6) s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off while the car is 70 m away at 12 m/s: no closest approach within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stays on the sidewalk throughout.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car is 12 m away at 12 m/s on a collision course, but whether the pedestrian's footprint overlaps the roadway or the sidewalk is not observed.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian steps off the sidewalk with no vehicle in the scene: the duty binds the pedestrian alone and is met.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hayward 1972; Swedish traffic conflict technique)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.driver_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: perception-reaction time of an alert driver to an expected hazard in the stopping-distance model
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping sight distance; perception-reaction studies

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a dry paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.6)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on a wet paved surface (coefficient of friction about 0.4)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

param_proposals.name: p.following_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: braking deceleration of a passenger vehicle on an icy or snow-covered surface (coefficient of friction about 0.1)
param_proposals.source: tire-pavement friction tables of accident reconstruction handbooks

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated,
pedestrians facing the signal
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal
and must be given
the right-of-way
by the drivers of all vehicles.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}'); 'in place' is a head present in the scene. 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control: dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'), traffic including pedestrians (DEF-NRS-484A-285: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles'), ties the head to the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (kinds st.roadway, st.lane). dev.governs is not used as a position.
'the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated' is the head's state walk (dev.pedestrian_signal state 'walk').

'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian. 'facing the signal': the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head / sign face') lies ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along the direction its body points (kin.heading, 'direction the body points'), within a cone and a reach. dev.position is used as the head's location, not as the place of a stop line or crossing, which its exclusion names.

'may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal' identifies the pedestrians the right-of-way is owed to: those on the roadway the head governs (rel.occupies of a st.roadway or st.lane region that head governs), facing the head, so moving toward it across the way. The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines') is crossed by traversing its roadway; the sidewalk the words of the sibling subparagraphs call a place of safety is no part of the crossing.

Giving the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'the right of one vehicle or pedestrian to proceed in a lawful manner in preference to another') is observed as the vehicle not reaching the pedestrian (no rel.contact) with its speed (kin.speed) bounded as the standard sets, as the index maps 'Yield'.
'the drivers of all vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence where the two approach 'under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: while the vehicle moves (speed above the halt tolerance), a predicted closest approach of the two centres within the conflict horizon at a centre distance below the conflict clearance is a danger of a crash in which the vehicle has not granted precedence

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), not engaged by LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian p (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), a pedestrian signal head d showing walk, and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs), with p's footprint overlapping r (rel.occupies), p facing d, and p not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A or LVMC_11_30_060_B. p faces d where, with Δ the vector from p's kin.position to d's dev.position and h p's kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach².

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal,
but must complete the crossing before the countdown timer gets to zero.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute when a timer is displayed'); 'such signals' regulate the crossing of the roadway they control, read through dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane, ... roadway'; traffic includes pedestrians, DEF-NRS-484A-285) on a roadway or lane (kinds st.roadway, st.lane).

'“Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with its countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

The pedestrian who proceeds across the highway under this indication is one whose footprint came onto the governed roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) while the head showed it, facing the head: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach — the direction of the signal. dev.position is not used as a crossing or a stop line.

Completing the crossing is having left the roadway or lane crossed: the pedestrian's footprint no longer overlaps it (rel.occupies). The countdown timer gets to zero at the end of the flashing interval it times, where the head stops showing the flashing indication with a countdown and shows dont_walk_steady (dev.pedestrian_signal states dont_walk_flashing with countdown, then dont_walk_steady).

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. The judged observation is the countdown's end for a pedestrian head d governing (dev.governs) a roadway or lane r: d shows dont_walk_steady here and showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown at the previous observation. The subject's latest entry onto r (the latest earlier observation at which its footprint came to overlap r, not overlapping it at the observation before; history bound: that entry, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed dont_walk_flashing with its countdown and the subject faced d, and d showed dont_walk_flashing with countdown at every observation from that entry to the previous one. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where the entry lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: At the countdown's end the subject's footprint does not overlap r (rel.occupies): it has completed the crossing.

narrowings.why: the countdown's reaching zero is read as the head's change from the flashing indication with countdown to the steady indication, which ends the interval the timer counts; the timer's displayed number is not read.
'complete the crossing' is read as the pedestrian's footprint having left the roadway or lane governed by the head; a pedestrian on a median or safety zone between roadways has left it.

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer,
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety before the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian ('such signals') is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faces: the head's location (dev.position, 'location of the device head') ahead of the pedestrian's position (kin.position) along its heading (kin.heading, 'direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and flashing but is not accompanied by a countdown timer' is the head's state dont_walk_flashing with no countdown attribute displayed.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Proceeding to cross the highway is coming onto the roadway or lane the head governs: the pedestrian's footprint comes to overlap it (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane). The highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095) includes the sidewalk, but the sibling words 'must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone' place the sidewalk outside the crossing, so the crossing begins on the roadway.
'a pedestrian' (the one excepted) is the same admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) borrows (1)'s words: 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto a roadway or lane (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while a pedestrian head (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing that roadway or lane (dev.governs) showed walk and the pedestrian faced it (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is not having returned to a sidewalk (rel.occupies of st.sidewalk) since that entry: the pedestrian is still in the crossing it began.

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths

segmentation.text: Whenever signals exhibiting the words “Walk,” “Don’t Walk,” “Wait” or similar symbols are in place, such signals indicate as follows:
While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated and steady
a pedestrian
may not proceed to cross the highway,
but a pedestrian
who entered the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2)
may continue to cross the highway
but must proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone if one is provided or other place of safety
as soon as possible.

elements.justification: Signals exhibiting 'Walk', 'Don't Walk', 'Wait' or similar symbols are pedestrian heads (dev.pedestrian_signal: 'a pedestrian head; state ∈ {walk, dont_walk_flashing, dont_walk_steady, dark}; countdown attribute'). The signal that indicates to a pedestrian is the head that governs the roadway or lane its crossing traverses (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls', traffic including pedestrians by DEF-NRS-484A-285; kinds st.roadway, st.lane) and that the pedestrian faced when it stepped onto it: dev.position ('location of the device head') ahead of kin.position along kin.heading ('direction the body points') within a cone and a reach. dev.position is not used as a stop line or crossing.
'illuminated and steady' is the head's state dont_walk_steady.
'a pedestrian' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian.

Entering the highway lawfully pursuant to subparagraph (1) or (2) borrows their words: (1) 'While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'; (2) 'While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal'. It is the pedestrian's latest step from a sidewalk (st.sidewalk) onto the roadway or lane r (rel.occupies of st.roadway / st.lane) made while the head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) governing r (dev.governs) showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the pedestrian faced d (dev.position ahead of kin.position along kin.heading within the cone and reach).
Continuing to cross is the pedestrian's footprint still overlapping r (rel.occupies) while d shows the steady indication.

Proceeding to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone or other place of safety is moving off the roadway or lane crossed: while the footprint overlaps r (rel.occupies), the pedestrian moves (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity'), at the pace the standard bounds. kin.speed is used as the magnitude of motion, not as acceleration.

operationalizations.convention: pedestrian clearance walking speed: a pedestrian still on the roadway after the steady indication proceeds as soon as possible where its speed is at least a floor well below the slow walking speed the clearance interval is timed for; lingering or halting on the roadway is below it

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (1)'s permission — the walk indication illuminated, the pedestrian facing the signal, proceeding across the highway in its direction — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (1)'s rule is a duty on drivers to give the right-of-way; whether that duty applied to some vehicle, held, or was complied with says nothing of how this pedestrian entered, so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Walk” indication or walking person symbol is illuminated, pedestrians facing the signal may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

compositions.why: It borrows the circumstances of subparagraph (2)'s permission — the flashing don't-walk indication accompanied by a countdown timer, the pedestrian proceeding across the highway in the direction of the signal — to qualify how the pedestrian entered. Subparagraph (2)'s rule is the duty to complete the crossing before the countdown ends; lawful entry under (2) does not depend on that later duty being complied with (the entry precedes it), so no rule of it is composed and the qualified fact is carried by this node's own atoms.
compositions.quote: While the “Don’t Walk” or “Wait” indication or an upraised hand symbol is illuminated, is flashing and is accompanied by a countdown timer, a pedestrian may proceed across the highway in the direction of the signal

applicability: The subject is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), not engaged by NRS_484B_287_1c, NRS_484B_287_1d, NRS_484B_287_1e, LVMC_11_30_060_A, LVMC_11_30_060_B, LVMC_11_30_140_B_o1 or LVMC_11_30_140_B_o2, with no vehicle v of the scene engaged by LVMC_11_46_030_o1 or LVMC_11_46_030_o2. There are a pedestrian head d (dev.pedestrian_signal) showing dont_walk_steady and a roadway or lane r governed by d (dev.governs) such that the subject's footprint overlaps r here and the subject's latest step from a sidewalk onto r (history bound: that step, searched back without other limit) was made while d showed walk, or dont_walk_flashing with its countdown, and the subject faced d. The subject faces d where, with Δ the vector from its kin.position to d's dev.position and h its kin.heading: h·Δ > 0, (h·Δ)² ≥ p.ped_signal_facing_cos² · (Δx² + Δy²), and Δx² + Δy² ≤ p.ped_signal_facing_reach². Where that step lies before the recording, applicability is unknown.
obligation: The subject's speed (kin.speed) is at least p.pedestrian_clearing_speed_min: it keeps moving off the roadway rather than lingering on it.

narrowings.why: 'proceed to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone ... or other place of safety' is read through the pedestrian's motion while still on the roadway; the direction it moves in (forward or back to the curb it left) is not read, and the kind of place reached is not checked.
'as soon as possible' is read as a speed floor at every observation on the roadway after the steady indication; the pedestrian's own ability (a slower walker) is not measured.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stepped onto r from the sidewalk facing d while d showed walk; d now shows dont_walk_steady and the pedestrian stands still (0.0 m/s) in the middle of r.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same, but the pedestrian walks on across r at 1.3 m/s.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: d shows dont_walk_steady and the pedestrian waits on the sidewalk, off r.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Same as forbid but the pedestrian's speed is not observed.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: The recording begins with the pedestrian standing on r while d shows dont_walk_steady; its step onto r is not recorded, so whether it entered lawfully cannot be told.
scenarios.boundary: the pedestrian's step from the sidewalk onto r, which lies before the recording

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_clearing_speed_min
param_proposals.convention: the speed below which a pedestrian still on the roadway counts as lingering rather than proceeding to a place of safety: about half the 3.0 ft/s (0.9 m/s) walking speed to which pedestrian clearance intervals are timed for slower pedestrians
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.06 pedestrian clearance walking speeds (3.5 ft/s, 3.0 ft/s for slower pedestrians)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a pedestrian signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08 (pedestrian signal heads placed at the far end of the crossing, in the pedestrian's line of sight)

param_proposals.name: p.ped_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a pedestrian signal head at which the head counts as the one across the crossing the pedestrian faces: a wide urban crossing (six lanes and a median, about 30 m) plus the head's set-back behind the far curb
param_proposals.source: MUTCD section 4E.08; AASHTO Green Book urban cross-section widths
